title: Who do occupational therapists work with | NHS inform
text:
Who do occupational therapists work with
Occupational therapists aim to support you to participate fully in everyday life, to manage the activities that you want and need to be able to do.
If you have ongoing health needs, the focus is on preventing more challenges and maintaining a good quality of life. This’ll allow you to do what’s important to you.
Support for everyone
Occupational therapists work with people of all ages, including children. They look at all parts of daily life, from the home, to school or the workplace.
It’s used to treat and manage a wide range of needs and conditions. This includes conditions that:
are present from birth
develop with age
are the result of an accident
are the result of a change in mental wellbeing
People with a health condition
Occupational therapy may be used to support many different needs and health conditions, including:
arthritis
autism
cancer
cerebral palsy
chronic fatigue syndrome
chronic pain
dyspraxia (developmental co-ordination disorder)
mental health
conditions like
depression
,
anxiety
and
schizophrenia
neurological conditions like
multiple sclerosis (MS)
,
Parkinson’s disease
,
functional neurological disorder
learning disabilities like
Down’s syndrome
stroke
People who are recovering from an accident, illness or operation
Rehabilitation helps you recover from an accident, illness or operation. Occupational therapists are key members of the rehabilitation team. They can help support your rehabilitation after:
a hip fracture
a
severe head injury
a
stroke
stabalisation of an addiction
a diagnosis of
dementia
experiencing changes to
mental wellbeing
Occupational therapists aim to improve your ability to carry out everyday tasks. They’ll also help you regain as much independence as possible.
People with mental health conditions
Occupational therapists can support your recovery from mental health conditions. They’ll use activities that aim to help improve your mental health. They can also help you develop skills and techniques to take part in everyday life.
Occupational therapy can help people achieve things that are important to them. For example, self-care, being a parent or leisure activities.
If you’re working, occupational therapy can support you to keep your job during periods of mental illness.
Children
Occupational therapy can help children reach their developmental and educational potential. For example, an occupational therapist can work with children to improve:
writing skills
participation in school
confidence to play with others
independence with daily tasks
To help with these things, an occupational therapist may develop a game or activity. Your child can then complete this each day. For example, focusing on a small goal, like better hand strength, may eventually help your child to hold a spoon, a pencil or dress themselves.
Older people
Occupational therapy may be used to address health conditions related to getting older.
With conditions like arthritis you may find certain movements are not as easy as they used to be, like getting out of bed in the morning. An occupational therapist can suggest equipment and adaptations to your home to help. They may also suggest new techniques to help with this kind of activity.
Occupational therapy can also provide devices and strategies to help your memory. This can help people living with conditions linked to aging, like
dementia
and
Alzheimer’s disease
.
Source:
Royal College of Occupational Therapists
